lines.text: Round five starts the clock on the day the money arrives, and runs for two years. Each campaign has all of its money on day zero. The facility is ready between day 60 and day 100, and the equipment is ordered on day zero: some of it used, chosen by a rule.

lines.text: Experiments also start on day zero, through partners, while the lab is built. Decisions made by people take time. The conventional lab's atomizer runs at most 8 times a week; the automated lab's runs around the clock once its cell is integrated. And the HPC computes candidates continuously. Every lead time, price and decision window here is a stand-in.

lines.text: Everything here is simulated: the alloys, the results, and every measurement, with modelled noise not yet calibrated on the lab's instruments. The facility window, every lead time, the used-equipment prices, the decision windows, the HPC allocation, and the atomizer's design cycle are assumptions and stand-ins. It shows how two lab designs and their policies interact in a model, not what the real lab will find.
